mainTopic: תחיית המתים, the dead that יחזקאל revived, and the miracles of the fiery furnace
overview: The עמוד first finishes the teaching of תנא דבי אליהו: the צדיקים who are brought back to life will never die again. While הקדוש ברוך הוא renews the world, they will fly over the water on eagle-like wings without growing tired. The גמרא asks why we do not learn the opposite from the dead that יחזקאל revived, and answers that this teaching holds the vision was only a משל. A ברייתא then brings several views: some say those dead really lived, sang, and died again. Others say it was only a משל. Still others say they went up to ארץ ישראל and had families, and רבי יהודה בן בתירא even says he is their descendant. Next, five אמוראים each say who those dead people were, ending with רבי יוחנן, who says they were beautiful youths killed by נבוכדנצר in בקעת דורא. A ברייתא tells how יחזקאל revived them on the day חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה were thrown into the furnace, and how this led נבוכדנצר to praise ה׳. The גמרא then lists six miracles from that day and learns from the three men's clothing that a person should keep his dignity even in danger. A new statement of רבי יוחנן begins at the end and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: What do the righteous do while the world is being renewed?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a question: if the revived צדיקים never die again, where are they during the years when הקדוש ברוך הוא renews the world?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will ask: during those years when the Holy One, Blessed be He, will renew His world, as the פסוק says, 'And the Lord alone shall be exalted on that day,' what will the righteous do?
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching of תנא דבי אליהו continues with a question. The next step will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier teaching said the צדיקים who come back to life never return to dust. The פסוק 'the Lord alone shall be exalted' suggests a time when only ה׳ remains while the world is renewed. So how can the צדיקים still be alive during that time?

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible question)

phrases.english: And if you say: those years
when the Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined
to renew His world during them,
as it is stated: "And the Lord alone shall be exalted on that day,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 2:11

phrases.english: what will the righteous do?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תֹּאמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier teaching of תנא דבי אליהו, which said that the revived צדיקים do not return to dust
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the revived צדיקים survive during the years when the world is renewed

steps.title: They are given eagle wings and fly over the water
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ gives the צדיקים wings like eagles, and they fly above the water while the land is being changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Holy One, Blessed be He, makes them wings like eagles, and they fly over the surface of the water, as the פסוק says: 'Therefore we will not fear when the land is changed, and when mountains are moved into the heart of the seas.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question. The צדיקים get wings and stay safe above the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in תהלים describes people who are not afraid even while the land changes and the mountains fall into the sea. They have nothing to fear because they are up in the air at that time. This way they stay alive, and the teaching that they never return to dust holds.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, makes for them
wings like eagles,
and they fly over the surface of the water,
as it is stated: "Therefore we will not fear
when the land is changed
and when mountains are moved into the heart of the seas."
phrases.notes: תהלים 46:3

steps.triggerLanguage: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה לָהֶם כְּנָפַיִם כִּנְשָׁרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ gives the צדיקים eagle wings, and they fly over the water while the world is renewed

steps.title: They will not suffer or get tired
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא heads off a worry that flying for so long would be painful. A פסוק in ישעיהו shows they will not tire.
steps.simpleTranslation: And perhaps you will say they will be in pain from flying so long? The פסוק teaches: 'Those who hope to the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall go up with wings like eagles; they shall run and not be weary; they shall walk and not tire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks one more possible question and answers it right away with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flying for years might seem exhausting. The פסוק in ישעיהו describes people who rise on eagle wings and never grow weary. So the flight causes the צדיקים no suffering at all.
steps.whatToRemember: According to תנא דבי אליהו, the צדיקים who are revived never die again. Even when the world is renewed, they fly above it on eagle wings and feel no pain.

phrases.english: And lest you say: they will have suffering?
The verse teaches: "Those who hope to the Lord shall renew their strength;
they shall go up with wings like eagles;
they shall run and not be weary;
they shall walk and not tire."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 40:31

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר: יֵשׁ לָהֶם צַעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises and answers a follow-up worry about the answer in step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The צדיקים will not suffer or get tired from flying

steps.title: Why not learn from the dead that יחזקאל revived?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges תנא דבי אליהו: the dead that יחזקאל revived died again, so maybe revived people do return to dust.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn from the dead that יחזקאל brought back to life, who died again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that revived people never die again, pointing to the dead in יחזקאל's prophecy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ספר יחזקאל, dry bones come back to life. If those people later died again, this would show that people who are brought back to life can die. That would go against what תנא דבי אליהו said.

keyTerms.meaning: Whom he brought back to life

phrases.english: And let us learn from the dead
whom Yechezkel revived?
phrases.notes: This is the story of the dry bones in יחזקאל 37. The גמרא assumes those people later died again.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵילַף מִמֵּתִים שֶׁהֶחְיָה יְחֶזְקֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the basic claim of תנא דבי אליהו that revived צדיקים never die
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of תנא דבי אליהו that people revived at תחיית המתים never return to dust
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The dead revived by יחזקאל died again, which shows that revived people can die

steps.title: He holds that יחזקאל's vision was a משל
steps.stepSummary: תנא דבי אליהו holds like the view that יחזקאל's revival of the dead was only a משל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like the one who says: in truth, it was a parable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. תנא דבי אליהו holds that the story of יחזקאל was not a real event.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no one was actually brought back to life, we cannot learn anything from it about real תחיית המתים. So the challenge falls away. The next steps bring the ברייתא where this view appears.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like the one who says

phrases.english: He holds in accordance with the one who says:
phrases.notes: "He" means תנא דבי אליהו, whose teaching we have been learning.

phrases.english: In truth, it was a parable.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying which side of a תנאים argument the teaching follows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dead in יחזקאל really lived and died again, which would prove that revived people die
steps.terutzMaskana: תנא דבי אליהו holds the vision was a משל, so nothing can be learned from it

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: they stood, sang, and died
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins. רבי אליעזר says the dead יחזקאל revived stood up, sang a song to ה׳, and died again.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר says, the dead that יחזקאל revived stood on their feet, said a song, and died. What song did they say? 'ה׳ kills with justice and gives life with mercy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that contains the view mentioned in step 5. It opens with רבי אליעזר, who says the event really happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אליעזר, the revival was real but lasted only a short time. This is exactly the view that would have caused the challenge in step 4, because these revived people died again.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Eliezer says:
The dead that Yechezkel revived
stood on their feet
and recited a song and died.
What song did they recite?
"The Lord kills with justice and gives life with mercy."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא in which the view cited in step 5 appears
steps.raayaObject: That there is a תנאים argument over whether יחזקאל's revival was real
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the views of רבי אליעזר, רבי יהושע, רבי יהודה and others

steps.title: רבי יהושע: a different song
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע agrees the event was real but says they sang the פסוק from חנה's song: 'ה׳ kills and gives life.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: this is the song they said: 'ה׳ kills and gives life; He brings down to the grave and brings up.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא agrees the revival really happened. He disagrees only about which song they sang.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע's song is a פסוק from שמואל א. Like רבי אליעזר, he treats the event as real, so these people also lived and then died.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
This is the song they recited:
"The Lord kills and gives life;
He brings down to the grave and brings up."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 2:6

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: שִׁירָה זוֹ אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion on which song they sang
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The revived dead sang 'ה׳ ממית ומחיה מוריד שאול ויעל'

steps.title: רבי יהודה: it was truth, a parable
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה describes the event with the puzzling words 'truth, a parable.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: it was truth, a parable.
steps.whatsHappening: A third view says the story was both 'truth' and 'a parable.' This sets up רבי נחמיה's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two words seem to clash. A real event is not usually called a משל, and a משל is not usually called a real event. The ברייתא will explain this next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
It was truth; it was a parable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֱמֶת מָשָׁל הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different view from רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, who held it was real
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vision of יחזקאל was 'אמת משל'

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: truth or parable, which is it?
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה challenges רבי יהודה's wording. Something cannot be both a real event and a משל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said to him: if it is true, why call it a parable? And if it is a parable, why call it true?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה attacks the wording 'truth, a parable' because it seems to contradict itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'True' means the event really happened, and 'parable' means it did not. Calling it both makes no sense, so the wording must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is true, why call it a parable?

steps.confusionAlert: רבי נחמיה is not rejecting רבי יהודה's view. He is pushing to make the wording clear, and in the next step he explains how to read it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya said to him:
If it was truth, why call it a parable?
And if it was a parable, why call it truth?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה: אִם אֱמֶת, לָמָּה מָשָׁל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of step 8

steps.title: It means: in truth, it was a parable
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה explains the phrase to mean 'in truth, it was only a משל.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means: in truth, it was a parable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה gives the correct reading: the word 'truth' simply means 'really,' and what really happened is that it was a משל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the exact view the גמרא mentioned in step 5. Since the dead never actually came back to life, nothing can be learned from them, and תנא דבי אליהו's teaching stands.
steps.whatToRemember: 'באמת משל היה' means the vision of the dry bones was only a משל. This is the view תנא דבי אליהו follows, so revived צדיקים are not shown to die again.

phrases.english: Rather, in truth it was a parable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, בֶּאֱמֶת מָשָׁל הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי נחמיה's own challenge in step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Truth' and 'parable' are two separate descriptions that contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Truth' means 'really,' so the meaning is: it really was only a parable

steps.title: They went up to ארץ ישראל and had families
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי says the revived dead lived full lives in ארץ ישראל, marrying and having children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר the son of רבי יוסי הגלילי says: the dead that יחזקאל revived went up to ארץ ישראל, married wives, and had sons and daughters.
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא goes the other way. The event was fully real, and the revived people lived long normal lives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of 'it was a parable.' Not only were they really brought back to life, they went on to build families.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, says:
The dead that Yechezkel revived
went up to Eretz Yisrael,
and married wives
and fathered sons and daughters.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the 'parable' view and goes further than רבי אליעזר's view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The revived dead were real people who lived on, married, and had children in ארץ ישראל

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בתירא: I am their descendant
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא stands up and says he descends from them, and he shows תפילין his grandfather left him that came from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירא stood on his feet and said: I am one of their descendants, and these are תפילין that my father's father left me from them.
steps.whatsHappening: A תנא offers living evidence that the revived dead really existed and had families. He is their descendant and has their תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words back up רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי. If he descends from them and owns their תפילין, the revival was real and long-lasting, not a משל.

keyTerms.meaning: From their descendants (literally, their children's children)

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא עַל רַגְלָיו
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira stood on his feet
and said: I am one of their descendants,
and these are tefillin
that my father's father left me from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמַד רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא עַל רַגְלָיו וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the view of step 11 with personal evidence
steps.raayaObject: That the dead revived by יחזקאל really lived on and had descendants
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה בן בתירא's family line and the תפילין he inherited from them

steps.title: Who were the dead that יחזקאל revived?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the identity of the dead people whom יחזקאל brought back to life.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who were the dead people that יחזקאל brought back to life?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple identity question: who were these dead people? It is setting up the next move, where five אמוראים will give different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about whether the event really happened and what happened to the people afterward. Now the focus moves to who they were in the first place. The question is open, so it leaves room for several answers.

keyTerms.meaning: The נביא יחזקאל, who saw the vision of the dry bones

phrases.english: And who are the dead whom Ezekiel revived?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the earlier discussion about whether the revival was real, and what the revived people did afterward, to who they were.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the dead people whom יחזקאל revived.

steps.title: רב: they were the sons of אפרים who miscounted the end of the exile
steps.stepSummary: רב says the dead were members of שבט אפרים who calculated the end of the exile in מצרים, got it wrong, and were killed. He brings פסוקים from דברי הימים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: These were members of שבט אפרים who counted toward the end of the exile and made a mistake. As the פסוק says: 'And the sons of אפרים: שותלח, and his son ברד, and his son תחת, and his son אלעדה, and his son תחת, and his son זבד, and his son שותלח, and עזר and אלעד, whom the men of גת who were born in the land killed.' And it is written: 'And אפרים their father mourned many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer. The dead were people from שבט אפרים who tried to leave מצרים too early and were killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק shows that a group of אפרים's sons was killed by the men of גת. The second פסוק shows that אפרים himself mourned them, so this happened during his lifetime, while בני ישראל were still in מצרים. According to רב, these are the bones יחזקאל later brought back to life.

keyTerms.meaning: The descendants of אפרים, the son of יוסף
The end, meaning the set time when the exile would end
And it is written, which brings a second פסוק

phrases.english: Rav says:
These were the descendants of Ephraim
who calculated the end and erred,
phrases.notes: They tried to figure out when the exile in מצרים would end, got it wrong, and left too early.

phrases.english: as it is stated: “And the sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 7:20–21

phrases.english: and Bered his son, and Tahath his son,
and Eleadah his son, and Tahath his son,
and Zabad his son, and Shuthelah his son,
and Ezer and Elead
whom the men of Gath slew
that were born in the land, etc.”,
and it is written: “And Ephraim their father mourned
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 7:22

phrases.english: many days,
and his brothers came to comfort him.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: אֵלּוּ בְּנֵי אֶפְרַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dead were members of שבט אפרים who miscounted the end of the exile in מצרים and were killed by the men of גת.

steps.title: שמואל: they were people who denied the resurrection of the dead
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the dead were people who denied תחיית המתים, based on the פסוק in יחזקאל where they say, 'Our bones are dried and our hope is lost.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: These were people who denied תחיית המתים. As the פסוק says: 'And He said to me: Son of man, these bones are the whole house of ישראל. Behold, they say: Our bones are dried up, our hope is lost, we are cut off.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different answer. The dead were people who did not believe the dead would ever come back to life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל reads the פסוק as describing what these people believed: once our bones are dry, there is no hope, and we are cut off for good. So the people in the vision are those who denied תחיית המתים.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
These were people
who denied the resurrection of the dead,
as it is stated: “Then He said to me: Son of man,
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 37:11

phrases.english: these bones
are the whole house of Israel;
behold, they say: Our bones are dried
and our hope is lost; we are cut off.”

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֵלּוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁכָּפְרוּ בִּתְחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 13, different from רב's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dead were people who denied תחיית המתים and said their hope was lost.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה בר אבא: they were people without any trace of מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא says the dead were people who had not even a bit of 'moisture' of מצוה in them, based on the words 'the dry bones.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: These were people who had not even a little 'moisture' of מצוה in them. As the פסוק says: 'The dry bones, hear the word of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה בר אבא gives a third answer. The dead were people who were completely empty of מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'dry bones' as describing how these people lived, not just how their bones looked after death. They were spiritually dry, with not one drop of מצוה. Even so, ה׳ called to them to hear His word and brought them back to life.

keyTerms.meaning: Moisture, a little bit of wetness

steps.whatToRemember: So far there are three opinions about who יחזקאל revived: רב says the sons of אפרים who left מצרים too early, שמואל says people who denied תחיית המתים, and רבי ירמיה בר אבא says people with no מצוות at all. רבי יצחק נפחא and רבי יוחנן add two more answers in the next steps.
steps.confusionAlert: Both שמואל and רבי ירמיה בר אבא build on the image of 'dry bones,' but in different ways. For שמואל it shows that the people had lost hope in תחיית המתים. For רבי ירמיה בר אבא it shows that they were dry of מצוות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba says:
These were people
in whom there was not the moisture of a מצוה,
phrases.notes: He means not even the smallest bit of מצוה, the way something completely dry has no moisture left.

phrases.english: as it is stated: “The dry bones,
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 37:4

phrases.english: hear the word of the Lord.”

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: אֵלּוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן לַחְלוּחִית שֶׁל מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer to the question of step 13, different from both רב and שמואל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dead were people with no trace of מצוה in them, described as 'dry bones.'

steps.title: The dead were those who filled the היכל with idol images
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא says the dead were people who covered the היכל with images of disgusting creatures. He links the two פסוקים through the shared word סביב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא says: These were people who covered the whole היכל with images of disgusting creatures and creeping things. The proof is the פסוק about images carved 'around' the wall, together with the פסוק about the bones, where it says 'around and around.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is another answer to the question from step 13: who were the dead that יחזקאל revived? רבי יצחק נפחא names a different group of sinners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים are in ספר יחזקאל, and both use the word סביב ('around'). The shared word tells us they are about the same people. So the bones belonged to the idol worshippers יחזקאל saw in the היכל.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary, the main building of the בית המקדש
Idols (a word of disgust for them)
Around; the shared word that links the two פסוקים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha says:
These are people
who covered the entire Sanctuary
with repugnant creatures and creeping animals,
as it is stated: "So I came and saw
and behold, every form of creeping animal
and repugnant animal
and all the idols of the house of Israel
etched upon the wall around, etc."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 8:10

phrases.english: and it is written there:
"And he passed me over them around and around."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 37:2, in the vision of the dry bones. The shared word סביב connects it to the first פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא אָמַר: אֵלּוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth answer to the same question, alongside those of רב, שמואל, and רבי ירמיה בר אבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dead were people who etched images of disgusting creatures all around the היכל, linked by the word סביב.

steps.title: The dead were the dead of בקעת דורא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the dead whom יחזקאל revived were the dead lying in בקעת דורא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: These were the dead who lay in בקעת דורא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a fifth answer to the question of who the dead were. He points to a specific place, בקעת דורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers described the dead by the sin they committed. רבי יוחנן instead identifies them by where they died. The next step explains who these dead were and how they got there.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
These are the dead who were in the Dura Valley.
phrases.notes: This is the same valley mentioned in דניאל פרק 3.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֵלּוּ מֵתִים שֶׁבְּבִקְעַת דּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to the same question, this time identifying the dead by location.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dead were those lying in בקעת דורא.

steps.title: The story of the beautiful youths killed by נבוכדנצר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains who the dead of בקעת דורא were. They were handsome Jewish youths whom נבוכדנצר killed and then had trampled, because the Babylonian women were drawn to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן also said: The bodies filled the whole valley from the Eshel River to Rabbat. When נבוכדנצר exiled the Jews, there were young men among them so beautiful they outshone the sun. The Babylonian women saw them and became sick with desire. The women told their husbands, and the husbands told the king. The king had the youths killed, but the women still desired them. So the king had their bodies trampled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds background to his answer. He tells the story of how so many dead came to lie in בקעת דורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after death the youths' beauty stayed, so killing them did not stop the women. נבוכדנצר then ordered the bodies trampled so their form could not be seen. These trampled bones are the dead יחזקאל later revived.

keyTerms.meaning: The wicked king of בבל who exiled the Jews
A flow of discharge, like that of a זבה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says:
From the Eshel River to Rabbat
is the Dura Valley,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהִגְלָה נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר הָרָשָׁע אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: for at the time that the wicked Nevuchadnetzar exiled Israel
there were young men among them
who put the sun to shame with their beauty,
and the Chaldean women would see them
and flow with discharge.
phrases.notes: This happened to them out of desire for the youths.

phrases.english: They told their husbands,
and their husbands told the king.
The king commanded, and they killed them,
and still the women were flowing with discharge.
The king commanded, and they trampled them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִנְּהַר אֵשֶׁל עַד רַבַּת בִּקְעַת דּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רבי יוחנן's answer by explaining who the dead of בקעת דורא were.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dead of בקעת דורא were beautiful Jewish youths killed and trampled by order of נבוכדנצר.

steps.title: יחזקאל revives the dead while the three are in the furnace
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה were thrown into the furnace, ה' sent יחזקאל to revive the dead of בקעת דורא. Seeing this, נבוכדנצר praised ה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When נבוכדנצר threw חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה into the fiery furnace, ה' told יחזקאל, 'Go revive the dead in בקעת דורא.' When he revived them, bones came and struck נבוכדנצר in the face. He asked, 'What are these?' They told him, 'The friend of these three is reviving the dead in בקעת דורא.' He then praised ה', saying, 'How great are His signs and how mighty His wonders; His kingdom is forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that tells the story of the revival of the dead in בקעת דורא. It fits with רבי יוחנן's view that these were the dead יחזקאל revived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two miracles happened at once: the three were saved in the furnace, and יחזקאל revived the dead. The bones striking the king made him ask, and once he heard the answer he praised ה'. The ברייתא reads נבוכדנצר's words in דניאל as his reaction to this revival.

keyTerms.meaning: The three Jewish men thrown into the furnace for refusing to bow to the idol
What is their nature? What are these?

steps.confusionAlert: 'The friend of these' does not mean a friend of the bones. 'These' means חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה, and their friend is יחזקאל.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
At the time that the wicked Nevuchadnetzar cast
Chananya, Mishael, and Azarya
into the fiery furnace,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִיחֶזְקֵאל:
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Yechezkel:
Go and revive the dead in the Dura Valley.
Once he revived them,
bones came

phrases.aramaic: וְטָפְחוּ לוֹ לְאוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע עַל פָּנָיו.
phrases.english: and struck that wicked man on his face.
He said: What is the nature of these?
They said to him:
The friend of these
phrases.notes: 'These' means חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה, and the friend is יחזקאל.

phrases.english: is reviving the dead in the Dura Valley.
He began and said:
"His signs, how great they are,
and His wonders, how mighty they are;
His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom
and His dominion is from generation to generation, etc."
phrases.notes: דניאל 3:33

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהִפִּיל נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר הָרָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the בקעת דורא line with a ברייתא describing the revival itself and נבוכדנצר's reaction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יחזקאל revived the dead of בקעת דורא at the time of the furnace, and this moved נבוכדנצר to praise ה'.

steps.title: רבי יצחק's harsh comment on נבוכדנצר's praise
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says molten gold should be poured into נבוכדנצר's mouth, because if an angel had not slapped him, his praises would have outshone all of דוד's songs in תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Let boiling gold be poured into that wicked man's mouth. If an angel had not come and slapped him on the mouth, he would have tried to outdo all the songs and praises that דוד said in ספר תהלים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק reacts to the praise נבוכדנצר said in the last step. He explains why that praise was dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נבוכדנצר's praise was so powerful that he was about to surpass דוד המלך's praises. An angel had to stop him by slapping his mouth. That a wicked king could nearly outshine דוד is why רבי יצחק speaks so harshly of him.

keyTerms.meaning: To put to shame, to outshine
The book of Psalms, written by דוד

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן and the ברייתא, the dry bones יחזקאל revived were the trampled youths of בקעת דורא. Their revival during the miracle of the furnace drew such great praise from נבוכדנצר that an angel had to stop him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Let boiling gold be poured
into the mouth of that wicked man,
for had an angel not come
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The meaning is the same either way.

phrases.english: and slapped him on his mouth,
he would have sought to put to shame
all the songs and praises
that David said in the book of Psalms.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: יוּצַק זָהָב רוֹתֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on נבוכדנצר's praise from the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נבוכדנצר's praise was so great that an angel had to stop him before he surpassed דוד's praises in תהלים.

steps.title: Six miracles happened on the day of the furnace
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists six miracles that took place on the day חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה were saved from the furnace.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Six miracles happened that day. The furnace floated up, the furnace broke open, its plaster melted away, the idol fell on its face, four groups of officials were burned, and יחזקאל revived the dead in בקעת דורא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists six miracles from the day of the furnace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last miracle on the list is the one we just learned about in step 20: יחזקאל reviving the dead of בקעת דורא. The list shows that this was one of several wonders that all happened on the same day.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'kingdoms'; here, groups of royal officials

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Six miracles were done on that day,
phrases.notes: 'That day' means the day חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה were thrown into the furnace.

phrases.english: and these are they: the furnace floated up,
and the furnace broke open,
and its plaster melted away,
phrases.notes: סוד here is the lime coating that held the furnace together.

phrases.english: and the idol fell over on its face,
and four groups of officials were burned,
phrases.notes: Literally 'four kingdoms.' The next step shows these are four ranks of the king's officials.

phrases.aramaic: וְהֶחְיָה יְחֶזְקֵאל אֶת הַמֵּתִים בְּבִקְעַת דּוּרָא.
phrases.english: and Ezekiel revived the dead in the Dura Valley.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁשָּׁה נִסִּים נַעֲשׂוּ בְּאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the furnace story from step 20 by listing all the miracles of that day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six miracles happened on the day of the furnace, including יחזקאל reviving the dead.

steps.title: Where we know the miracles from, and the proof for the four groups
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says all six miracles are known from tradition, except the burning of the four groups of officials, which is learned from פסוקים in דניאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We know all of them from tradition, but the four kingdoms come from a פסוק. First, eight ranks of officials are gathered. Later, after the three men come out of the fire, only four ranks are mentioned as seeing them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the source for the list of miracles and proves one of them, the burning of four groups of officials, from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the start, נבוכדנצר gathers eight ranks of officials. After the miracle, only four of those ranks are named as gathering to see the men. The missing four ranks must have been burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a received tradition, not something read in a פסוק

phrases.english: And all of them are known by tradition,
and the four kingdoms are from a verse.
As it is written: "And Nebuchadnezzar the king sent
phrases.notes: דניאל 3:2

phrases.english: to gather the satraps, the prefects, and the governors,
the counselors, the treasurers, the judges, the magistrates,
and all the rulers of the provinces, etc."
phrases.notes: Count them: with this one, the פסוק lists eight ranks of officials.

phrases.english: And it is written: "There are certain Jewish men"
phrases.notes: דניאל 3:12

phrases.english: And it is written: "And the satraps, the prefects, and the governors gathered,
phrases.notes: דניאל 3:27

phrases.aramaic: וְהַדָּבְרֵי מַלְכָּא חָזַיִן לְגֻבְרַיָּא אִלֵּךְ וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and the king's counselors, seeing these men, etc."
phrases.notes: Now only four ranks are named, so the other four must have been burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלְּהוּ גְּמָרָא, וְאַרְבַּע מַלְכִיּוֹת קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the list in step 22 and proves the fifth miracle from the פסוקים.
steps.raayaObject: That four groups of officials were burned in the furnace miracle
steps.raayaSupportSource: דניאל 3:2 lists eight ranks, while דניאל 3:27 names only four ranks after the miracle.

steps.title: Keeping one's dignity even in danger
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב teaches that a person should keep his dignified status even in danger, learning it from the fine clothing the three men wore into the furnace.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב taught: Even in a time of danger, a person should not give up his dignified status. As it says: "Then these men were tied up in their cloaks, their tunics, and their hats."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a lesson about behavior, learned from a detail in the furnace story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק points out that the three men went into the fire still wearing their important clothing. From this we learn that a person of standing should not lower himself, even when his life is in danger.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the study hall of

steps.whatToRemember: Even in danger, a person should not give up his dignity. The source is the three men going into the furnace in their fine clothes.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov taught:
Even at a time of danger,
a person should not change himself
from his dignified status,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some leave it out. The meaning is the same either way.

phrases.english: as it is said: "Then these men
phrases.notes: דניאל 3:21

phrases.english: were tied up in their cloaks,
their tunics, and their hats, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב: אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁעַת הַסַּכָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the miracles to a lesson about behavior, drawn from the same furnace story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even in danger, a person should not give up his dignified status.

steps.title: Introducing a new statement of רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new statement from רבי יוחנן. The statement itself continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is only a setup. The גמרא is introducing רבי יוחנן, and his actual words come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the name of the speaker appears here. What he teaches comes on the next עמוד, so wait for it before drawing any conclusion.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching. The content continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduction only. רבי יוחנן's statement follows in the next lines.
